problem: Embodied capabilities (localization, navigation, spatial/embodied reasoning, memory-based planning) are handled by siloed specialist models. Stacking them is costly and error-prone, and navigation specialists such as InternVLA-N1 collapse out of domain through catastrophic forgetting.
motivation: Real robots need all of these skills at once, and a multi-model stack adds latency, complexity and cascading failures. The authors argue one planner VLM trained on a curated, spatially biased mixture with a simple memory harness can replace the stack without losing benchmark performance.
key_idea: Fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B on a large curated SFT mixture (spatial, navigation, grounding, general VLM, embodied reasoning, real-robot data) plus a minimalist image+text memory harness, giving a single generalist embodied planner.
insight: Unified training matches or beats specialists in their own domains (Table 'Generalist vs specialist': unified R2R-CE SR 55.5 vs 54.1 for nav-only; embodied cognition 70.5 vs 64.3 for embodied-only), which suggests positive transfer. In the memory ablation, image-only memory switches subtasks prematurely and text-only memory over-predicts 'continue', while the image+text hybrid is best (75.9 overall). Uniform vs recency-biased frame sampling perform about the same, so the memory modality mix matters more than the sampling policy.
method: Base model and SFT: full-parameter fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct for 1 epoch (LR 1e-5, 128 H100s, batch 256) on one mixture: Spatial Intelligence 27.1%, Navigation 21.8%, Grounding 20.8%, General VLM 16.2%, Embodied Reasoning 9.8%, Real Robots 4.3%.

Localization data: a base-tail design. The base is Objects365, COCO and LVIS; the tail is egocentric, manipulation-centric and temporal robot data. Points and boxes are emitted as text tokens through the ordinary language head.

Navigation: R2R-style VLN with InternNav-style outputs (pixel-goal waypoints in [0,1000]^2, turn sequences, or STOP), conditioned on the instruction, the current view and up to N sampled history frames. Data come from R2R, RxR and ScaleVLN rendered in Habitat, and low-level motion is handled by a backend.

Embodied reasoning: affordance and placement prediction, manipulation trajectories as waypoints, and progress estimation from egocentric video, trained on top of large-scale VQA, detection and pointing data.
Action planning with CoT: the model predicts the next subtask as text after a four-phase chain of thought (Observation, Progress, Reasoning, Action). Only the action is written to memory.

Memory harness: history images are capped at K by uniform or recency-biased sampling (first frame always kept) and interleaved with a running text log of past subtasks. Transition-phase steps are oversampled 2x.

Planner-actor deployment: the planner sends text subtasks to a Gr00t-N1.6 VLA actor, in synchronous or asynchronous mode. An offline MCQ planning benchmark scored with temporal IoU is used for cheap evaluation.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (full fine-tuned); Gr00t-N1.6 as low-level actor in real-robot tests
setting.training_data: Curated SFT mixture (six categories: spatial intelligence, navigation, grounding, general VLM, embodied reasoning, real robots), including R2R/RxR/ScaleVLN VLN-CE data, Objects365/COCO/LVIS, and real-robot/human-manipulation data; total scale not stated
setting.observation: Egocentric monocular RGB (current frame plus sampled history frames), text instruction/goal
setting.action_space: Navigation: pixel-goal waypoints, turn primitives (left/right) and STOP, with a low-level backend; planning: text subtasks
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport3D/HM3D scenes) for navigation; real bimanual I2RT YAM robot

numbers.extra: unified generalist SFT mix incl. embodied and general data; val-unseen scenes/episodes excluded from SFT

numbers_note: Non-navigation benchmarks are not among the canonical names, so only the R2R-CE numbers are listed. Vesta's embodied results (cognition avg 68.7, localization avg 69.9, offline planning avg 75.4) are in the tables but omitted here. Real-robot success rates appear only in a figure; the text gives +38.3% over actor-only and +25% over the Qwen3-VL planner.
results: On R2R-CE val-unseen Vesta reaches SR 55.5 and OS 61.4, on par with the InternVLA-N1 specialist (SR 55.4, SPL 52.1, NE 4.89) and far above generalists that score 0 SR. It has the best average on embodied cognition (68.7) and localization (69.9), and scores 75.4 on the offline planning benchmark versus 38.5 for the best baseline (RoboBrain-2.5). On real robots it improves success by 38.3% over an actor-only baseline.
limitations: Real-robot evaluation covers one platform (bimanual YAM) and three tabletop memory tasks, with no specialist baselines compared.
Only the 8B scale is studied, and the memory harness is a fixed sampling and text log rather than a learned memory.

Vesta trails on SPL and NE against InternVLA-N1 and on some benchmarks (VSI-Bench, RoboSpatial). The offline planning benchmark is partly internal (Egocentric Human-Hand), and the data mixture is not fully specified.
